assessment_copy.instructions_md:
# Pipeline Insights Console

## Overview

You are working on a telemetry analysis tool for a data platform that ingests events from batch sync jobs and live streams.

The project is already scaffolded as a normal TypeScript package. Your job is to understand the batch and streaming code paths, then extend the reporting layer without breaking the existing summaries.

## Core task

Improve the pipeline report in `src/report.ts` so it better combines batch summaries with stream-window insights.

The code should:
- summarize event volume, lateness, and failures by pipeline
- process the same events through an object-mode stream transform
- surface a deterministic CLI report for the bundled sample data
- keep the current tests green while preserving the data model

## Candidate workflow

- Read the types and sample telemetry to understand the domain.
- Run the test suite to see how batch and stream processing are exercised.
- Update the reporting layer without changing the surrounding project structure.
- Make sure the CLI output still reads cleanly.

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
npm run test
```

## Notes

- Batch summaries should be stable and reproducible.
- Stream processing should operate on object-mode events, not raw text.
- The project is intentionally small, but it models a real analytics workflow.

variation_axes.description: How the pipeline treats events that arrive after their window has already been emitted. drop discards them; re_bucket_by_event_time retroactively updates the original bucket; side_output_queue captures them in a separate late-arrivals channel.

How alerting thresholds are computed. absolute_count fires when raw failure count exceeds N; percentage_of_window fires when failure ratio exceeds X%; ema_smoothed uses an exponential moving average to suppress spiky false positives.
